title: Where du'as are accepted
summary: Hazrat's lesson from the story of Hazrat Zakariya and Bibi Maryam: the court of the awliya of Allah is a place where du'as are accepted. And why du'a is the core of worship.

blocks.h: Du'a is the core of worship

blocks.p: Hazrat often reminds his listeners that we worship but forget to ask. He explains the command Ud'uni astajib lakum: 'ask of Me; I will answer you'.

blocks.q: Ad-du'a mukhkh al-'ibadah: du'a is the core of worship. The worship we do is completed by du'a.
Your work is only to pray. Allah's work is to give. I am the one who prays; Allah is the One who gives.

blocks.p: In part 8, Hazrat tells the story of Bibi Maryam. Her parents had vowed to give their child to the service of Allah's house, and she was given a room in the place of worship, where Hazrat Zakariya, her uncle, looked after her.

One day, while they spoke near her room, a gust of wind lifted the curtain, and Hazrat Zakariya saw fruits inside that were out of season. He asked where they came from. She said: 'Allah sends them to me.'

blocks.q: Then, standing right there, he said: Ya Allah, You give Maryam fruit out of season. Now have mercy on me, be generous to me: give me a child out of season.

blocks.p: Allah accepted his du'a at once, and Jibreel brought him the news of a son, Hazrat Yahya. Hazrat points out where this happened: the du'a was made beside Bibi Maryam's room, and she is a waliya of Allah.

blocks.q: The house of Allah is for everyone. But whomever Allah calls His wali, His friend, and is kind to: that is his honour, his good fortune.
The court of the awliya of Allah is the place where Allah accepts du'as. Keep this in mind.

blocks.note: Parts 6 to 9 are not yet public on YouTube, so these passages have no video link yet. Ask your teacher about the adab of making du'a at the courts of the awliya.
